newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Wereldhave looking to sell Carnaby St site.
newsitem.headline: Wereldhave looking to sell Carnaby St site.

text.p: Dutch property fund Wereldhave said on Monday it was touting for buyers willing to pay "an extremely good price" for its extensive Carnaby Street retail site in central London.
"We're looking to see what it's worth," Wereldhave spokesman Peter Neervoort said. "If we get a very good offer we will consider selling."

Neervoort declined to confirm a report in Monday's Financial Times newspaper that Wereldhave was seeking at least 69 million sterling ($107.7 million) for the site, saying only the fund had instructed estate managers Healey & Baker to gauge market interest.
Carnaby Street, a pedestrianised city-centre shopping precinct, became renowned around the world during London's "swinging sixties" for street-wise style.

The Financial Times said the sell-off of the three-acre Carnaby Street site was part of a strategic shift by Wereldhave out of shops and offices and into housing and apartment complexes, but this was dismissed by Neervoort as "ridiculous".

At end-June Wereldhave's 2.4 billion guilder ($1.44 billion) property portfolio comprised 48 percent offices, 43 percent retail properties and nine percent "other properties" including factory units, Neervoort said.
